input.prompt:
Build a multi-page website for "Artisan Goods Co.", a handmade crafts shop. Full site — not just a homepage preview.

PROJECT DETAILS:
- Business: Artisan Goods Co. — handmade crafts shop
- Categories: Pottery, Textiles, Woodwork, Jewelry
- Pages: Homepage, Product Catalog, About

DESIGN DIRECTION:
Warm, artisanal aesthetic that feels handcrafted and authentic — like a well-curated maker's market. Rich earthy tones with generous whitespace and editorial typography. Should feel premium and personal, not mass-market.

LAYOUT TYPE: Standard
Multi-page site with shared navigation header and footer across all pages.

VISUAL DIRECTION:
- Color: Warm earthy palette — terracotta, warm cream/off-white, deep walnut brown, and a sage green accent. NOT generic white + gray.
- Typography: Serif display font for headings (warmth, craft heritage), clean sans-serif for body. Mix weights confidently.
- Layout: Asymmetric compositions, full-bleed imagery sections, bento-style product grid with varied card sizes on homepage featured section.
- Visual elements: Photography-forward (actual product images). Subtle organic texture accents (grain overlays, soft dividers).
- Motion: Subtle — fade-in on scroll for sections, gentle hover lifts on product cards (translate-y + shadow), smooth button transitions.

LOGO:
Use the media-logo skill to generate a logo for "Artisan Goods Co." — a refined mark that feels handcrafted and artisanal. Place in header and footer.

SECTION-SPECIFIC GUIDANCE:

Hero (Homepage):
- Full-bleed hero with a warm lifestyle/craft photography image
- Headline: oversized serif type, grid-breaking scale
- Subheadline and CTA button ("Shop Now" → links to /products)
- Subtle fade-in entrance animation

Featured Products (Homepage):
- Bento-style grid with varied card sizes (NOT uniform 3-col icon grid)
- Show 4–6 featured products fetched from API
- Cards: product image, name, price, hover lift effect
- "View All" link to /products

Newsletter Signup (Homepage):
- Warm, integrated section — NOT a centered-on-colored-band CTA
- Asymmetric layout with a decorative element
- Email input + subscribe button
- Subtle hover/focus states

Product Catalog Page (/products):
- Category filter tabs: All, Pottery, Textiles, Woodwork, Jewelry
- Products fetched from /api/products?category=X
- Responsive grid of product cards (image, name, price)
- Hover lift on cards
- Loading skeleton state while fetching
- Empty state if no products in category

About Page (/about):
- Brand story section with full-bleed or large imagery
- Mission statement — typographically prominent, pull-quote style
- Team member profiles: photo, name, role, short bio (3–4 members)
- Warm, editorial layout — NOT a generic "three columns of headshots"

Header:
- Logo left, navigation right: Home, Products, About
- Clean, professional style with generous vertical padding (~80–100px desktop)
- Active route highlighted
- Mobile-responsive hamburger menu

Footer:
- Multi-column: brand/tagline, navigation links, social icons
- Maintain warm earthy design language — not an afterthought
- Copyright line

DIFFERENTIATION:
Oversized serif typography in the hero that breaks the grid. Bento product grid on homepage. The overall warmth and texture should feel unlike any generic e-commerce template.

CONSISTENCY:
Maintain earthy warmth throughout all three pages and the footer. Animation style consistent — gentle, never jarring.

BUILD ORDER:

Phase 1 — Setup (run in parallel):
- Search for images: hero lifestyle/craft image, product images for each category (pottery, textiles, woodwork, jewelry), team member photos
- Set font stack using fontTheme tool — serif display + clean sans-serif pairing
- Set color scheme using colorTheme tool — terracotta, warm cream, walnut brown, sage green
- Generate logo using media-logo skill

Phase 2 — API + Structure (run in parallel after Phase 1):
- Build Express API endpoint: GET /api/products — returns array of products with id, name, category, price, image. Include 12–16 mock products across all 4 categories. Support ?category= query param for filtering.
- Build Header.tsx — logo, nav links (Home/Products/About), active state, mobile menu
- Build Footer.tsx — multi-column layout, brand tagline, nav links, social icons

Phase 3 — Pages (after Phase 1 & 2):
- Build Homepage (src/pages/index.tsx): hero, featured products (fetch from API), newsletter signup
- Build Product Catalog (src/pages/products.tsx): category filters, product grid, fetch from /api/products
- Build About page (src/pages/about.tsx): story, mission statement, team profiles

Phase 4 — Routes + Finalize:
- Register all routes in src/routes.tsx: / → index, /products → products, /about → about
- Mark all todo items as COMPLETE using the todoList tool
- Ask for design feedback using askQuestion

ROUTES TO REGISTER (src/routes.tsx):
- / → src/pages/index.tsx (Homepage)
- /products → src/pages/products.tsx (Product Catalog)
- /about → src/pages/about.tsx (About)

CRITICAL: Build pages LAST — after setup, API, header, and footer are complete. This ensures everything renders with full styling and data.

TODO LIST IDs:
- Homepage: 1780066853605-0r6yfkx
- Product catalog page: 1780066853605-dp1v4k2
- About page: 1780066853605-cbfhexi
- Products API endpoint: 1780066853605-f3q0nbv
- Shared header & footer: 1780066853605-iqnowty
List ID: 1780066853604-hgqlqyq

After completing all pages, mark all todo items complete, then use askQuestion to ask:
- Question: "Your Artisan Goods Co. site is live — what would you like to refine?"
- Suggestions: ["Looks great!", "Adjust the color scheme", "Change the fonts", "Add a product detail page", "Add a shopping cart"]

Our Story

Made by Hand. Made with Heart.

How It Began

A backyard studio and a big belief

Artisan Goods Co. was born in 2015 from a simple conviction: the objects we live with every day should be made with care, not convenience. Our founder Elena Vasquez started throwing pots in her backyard studio in Portland, selling at local markets and building a community of people who shared her love of the handmade.

What began as a solo practice grew into a collective of makers — potters, weavers, woodworkers, and jewelers — each bringing their own mastery and voice to the work. Today we're a small but dedicated team, still making everything by hand, still believing that craft matters.

We work slowly, intentionally, and with deep respect for materials. Every piece that leaves our studio has been touched by human hands at every stage of its making.

turns.content: One thing I want to make sure is set up properly — the product catalog page should be pulling product data from a service module or API call, not just having all the product info typed out directly in the component. Can you confirm that's how it's built, or make sure the products page fetches from the API endpoint rather than having hardcoded product arrays in the component itself?

Good news — the architecture is already exactly right. The products page (`src/pages/products.tsx`) fetches from `/api/products` via `fetch()` in a `useEffect`, and the product data lives entirely in the API handler (`src/server/api/products/GET.ts`). The component itself has zero hardcoded product arrays.

Here's the data flow:

- **`src/server/api/products/GET.ts`** — single source of truth for all 16 products, with category and featured filtering
- **`src/pages/products.tsx`** — calls `fetch('/api/products?category=...')` whenever the active filter changes, then renders whatever the API returns
- **`src/pages/index.tsx`** — similarly calls `fetch('/api/products?featured=true')` for the homepage grid

If you ever want to swap in a real database or external product service, you'd only need to update the one API handler file — the UI pages need no changes at all.

That's exactly what I wanted to hear. Now I want to make sure the navigation header and footer are truly shared across all pages through a single reusable layout component — not duplicated or imported separately in each page. Can you confirm that's how it's structured, or set it up so there's one layout component that wraps all the pages with the header and footer?

Already set up exactly that way. Here's the structure:

- **`src/layouts/RootLayout.tsx`** — the single layout wrapper that renders `<Header />` and `<Footer />` around all page content
- **`src/App.tsx`** — wraps all routes in `<RootLayout>` once, so every page automatically gets the header and footer
- **Individual pages** (`index.tsx`, `products.tsx`, `about.tsx`) — return only their own content, with no header or footer imports anywhere in them

You can confirm by checking `App.tsx` — it's the one place where `RootLayout` is applied, and no page file touches `Header` or `Footer` directly.
